newsitem.title: USA: Guzman & Co sues Gary & Co over Miami muni letter.
newsitem.headline: Guzman & Co sues Gary & Co over Miami muni letter.

text.p: Brokerage firm Guzman & Co filed suit against another Miami bond firm, Howard Gary & Co, claiming it forged a letter that resulted in lost municipal bond business for Guzman, according to court documents.
The lawsuit was filed Thursday in Dade County Circuit Court.
It accused Gary & Co. of libel, malicious interference with a business relationship, and forging and faxing a letter on Guzman & Co stationery.

The suit did not specify how much in damages it is seeking, but urged the court to consider "special damages" against Gary & Co and co-defendants Kishor Parekh, a senior vice president at Gary & Co; his father Manubhai Parekh; and the elder Parekh's firm, British Realty & Mortgage Corp.
The lawsuit accused the defendants of forging a letter that prompted Dade County to dismiss Guzman & Co from a $440 millon water-sewer bond issue.
It said the firm's dismissal "was either intended by the defendants in forging and faxing the letter or was a reasonably foreseeable result of their actions."
Earlier on Thursday, Gary & Co issued a statement denying involvement in the alleged forgery.

The letter at issue in the lawsuit accused one of Dade County's financial advisers, Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc, of violating a regulation against passing on certain municipal underwriting fees to issuers. It was written on Guzman & Co letterhead and purportedly signed by company president Leo Guzman.

Rauscher Pierce denied the allegation and Guzman insisted he did not write the letter. But county commissioners dismissed his firm from the bond deal anyway, saying that because of the letter "there is a shadow cast" on Guzman.
Guzman said Wednesday that phone records show a fax transmission of the letter was made from the Miami home of Manubhai Parekh.

Howard Gary, president of Howard Gary & Co, released a statement Thursday saying that the firm "considers the recently publicized events regarding a purportedly forged letter on Guzman & Co's letterhead as odious and offensive."

"Although Howard Gary & Co was not a participant in this activity, it expresses its empathy to Guzman & Co and Raushcer Pierce Refsnes Inc for the problems and inconveniences such false accusations and allegations have caused. This industry should have no place for such contemptible acts," the statement said.
Gary's firm was also dismissed from the Dade County bond deal because of concerns about Gary's role as a government witness in a federal probe of public finance corruption.
The deal was priced Thursday by PaineWebber Inc.
